grade.lesson: A well-defined, low-delta credit spread on a quiet mega-cap can still bleed a large fraction of its max profit in under 3 days from ordinary short-term IV/price noise, so size and monitor for early mark-to-market drawdowns even when the invalidation price level hasn't been breached.

thesis.rejected: Rejected buying DIS calls (needs a directional move, pays theta into a quiet tape); rejected semis premium selling (AMAT/MU/AMD IV 55-70% but wide $3-6 bid/ask and huge notional per contract, one adverse gap would exceed half the account); rejected an INTC or HOOD credit spread — attractive IV but both are in sharp momentum regimes where 5-10% daily moves are routine.
thesis.thesis: DIS is range-bound near $106 with low realized/implied vol (~21%) and no earnings before the 8/28 expiry. A 103/100 put credit spread expires worthless as long as DIS holds above $103, a 3.2% cushion over 14 calendar days. Theta and the elevated put skew on a slow-moving mega-cap are the edge.
thesis.why_this_structure: Short put vertical is fully defined risk ($300 width minus credit), margin-efficient in a small account, and expresses 'DIS does not fall 3%+ in two weeks' rather than needing an up-move. Selling naked puts would risk assignment on 100 shares; buying calls would need direction and pay theta.

grade.lesson: A well-reasoned, properly-sized defined-risk credit spread can still lose money quickly on adverse movement toward the short strike, and the trade should be judged on whether the stated stop-loss (2.5x credit or breach of $103) was actually followed rather than on the small dollar loss itself.

thesis.getting_paid: Credit ~$0.30 on a $3.00-wide spread = $30 collected, $270 max loss, ~11% return on risk in 14 days. Breakeven at $102.70 (-3.3%). Short strike delta ~0.22 implies ~78% probability of full profit; expected value is positive if the true probability of finishing below $103 is under ~90%/... precisely, EV>0 as long as P(full loss) < ~10% and P(expire worthless) > ~78%, which the delta already implies.
thesis.invalidation: Wrong if DIS closes below $103.00 on any day before 2026-08-28; I will close the spread for a loss if DIS trades below $103 or the spread's mark reaches ~2.5x the credit received (~$0.75), whichever comes first.
thesis.key_risk: A sharp market-wide risk-off move or a DIS-specific headline (streaming subscriber news, guidance leak, management change) that takes the stock through $103 quickly; the spread can lose the full $270, roughly 9x the credit collected.
thesis.rejected: Rejected long stock (no defined risk, ties up too much of a $2k account). Rejected buying cheap SPY/QQQ options (IV is low but I have no directional edge and theta is brutal into a 5-day expiry). Rejected selling AAL/INTC premium despite far higher IV — those names carry genuine event/solvency tail risk that justifies the IV. Rejected an iron condor on DIS because the call side pays only pennies and doubles commission/assignment complexity for negligible extra credit.
thesis.thesis: DIS trades at $106.16 in a calm tape (SPY near highs, index IV single digits). The Aug-28 103 put is ~22 delta with ~3% of downside cushion and only 14 days to expiry; the empirical odds of a >3% two-week decline in a low-beta media/parks name with no earnings before Aug 28 are well below the ~25% the option market is charging. Time decay works for me every day DIS holds above $103.
thesis.why_this_structure: A defined-risk credit spread caps loss at $270 in a $2,000 account, which naked short puts or long stock could not do. I chose puts over calls because the skew pays better on the downside and the drift/carry is with me. Width kept at $3 so max loss stays ~13% of equity; only one contract to keep sizing conservative in a small account.

thesis.thesis: CVS at 94.19 carries the lowest implied vol in my entire shortlist (~26% on Sep expiries vs 50-100% for AMAT/MU/MRVL/LRCX) with no earnings before Sep 25 and a steady grind higher. Low IV means long premium is cheap here rather than expensive, so the efficient expression of a mild bullish drift is a debit call vertical: pay ~2.45 for 7.00 of width on the Sep-25 96/103, giving me ~1.86:1 on capped risk with a 5-week window for a $4-9 move in a $94 stock (a ~4-9% move, well within CVS's realized range).
thesis.why_this_structure: A 96/103 debit vertical rather than a naked long call: the 103 short leg returns 0.38/share (15% of the long's cost) and caps upside at a level CVS is unlikely to blow through in 5 weeks, cutting theta bleed and cost basis. Max loss is the 735 debit, no assignment risk on a covered short, and options buying power (1,494) comfortably covers it. A credit spread was rejected because 26% IV is a poor price to sell.

grade.lesson: When the stock reverses back toward its 20-day average exactly as the thesis's own invalidation defined, cutting the long call there — rather than hoping for a rebound to expiry — is the correct discipline even though it locks in most of the premium loss.

I chose Sep-18 (25 DTE) over Sep-04 (11 DTE) because the front week's theta is -0.094/day against -0.061 here for a similar delta — the extra two weeks buys the thesis time to work rather than being taxed away. I chose the 111 strike (ATM, delta 0.55) rather than an OTM strike so the position tracks the move rather than needing a gap.

Implied vol ~34% is the name's normal level for oilfield services (last earnings 38 days ago, next 53 days away, so nothing is inflating or deflating it), which means I'm neither overpaying for an event nor buying vol that has just been crushed.
thesis.why_this_structure: With $1,114 of buying power a plain ATM long call on any of these names is 3-25% of the account for a single directional bet. The 1-wide vertical caps risk at $65 (5.4% of equity) while still paying 54% on risk if SLB holds $60. The short 60 leg does real work here — it funds ~40% of the long leg's cost and cuts theta drag, which matters because this is a hold-what-you-have thesis, not a breakout thesis. 59/60 are also the only two SLB strikes with tight two-sided quotes (2-7 cents wide), so the fill is realistic.
